limits: Synthetic native-touch Chromium portrait emulation with software WebGL

Captures release contacts and pause; automatic ~3s live / ~1.2s FIRE boundaries shorten waits. These do not establish human reaction timing, continuous held-burst rearming comfort or causal quality benefits.
Physical phones, Safari, audio, hardware performance and continuous enjoyment unassessed.

Every capture used default release-before-live-capture and pause; no captureHeld used. Both capture modes would break continuous holds. Frequent paused observation may aid deliberation but no human reaction-time or causal game-quality benefit is inferred.
Automatic release cannot establish continuous held-burst rearming comfort. Pausing can close KIT and clear AIM; neither KIT nor AIM-toggle behavior was tested.
Terminal mission times are game-displayed times under this interrupted workflow, not wall-clock completion or hardware performance measurements.
Supplied frozen commit was not verified because source inspection was prohibited; only visible BUILD 131 identity confirmed.

method.input: JSON-lines helper native CDP two-contact touch only
method.identity: BUILD 131 visibly confirmed at title; supplied source hash not independently inspected
method.scope: Only helper --help read for operation. No source, tests, docs, prior reviews, recordings, internal game state or target metadata inspected. Own report and evidence only.
method.attemptLifecycle: act tap #deploy + capture; after attempt-one terminal and saved incomplete report, act tap #play-again + capture; no checkpoint retry or third attempt.
method.observation: Every captured image viewed in a separate image-view call before dependent adaptive input. Waits at most 12000ms; shortened observationBoundary waits respected.

learningBetweenAttempts: Route changes into approach/recover at receivers, then directs to coils and deck.
Coil HUD independently identifies each disabled coil; screen projection shifts after target taps, so each next target chosen only from a fresh image.
Automatic reload occurs on empty; second run still exhausted a magazine on final coil and required waiting.
Carried this procedural knowledge into second run; terminal score difference is not evidence of a causal quality or reaction-time benefit.

observedHelpfulMoments.observation: Opening tip explains tap guard, FIRE, scene swipe and DASH; large bottom controls are labeled and reachable in emulated portrait view.
Route chevrons, HOLD APPROACH / HOLD TO RECOVER and checked name chips kept the next objective understandable.
Map fit the portrait screen with clear selected destination, route and legend.
Coil percentages/OFF labels, reload text and uplink progress gave actionable status feedback; terminal assist counts transparently disclosed assistance.

observedFrustrationsAndUncertainties: Distant humanoids were small in dark, visually similar industrial lanes; target brackets and directional HUD cues did much of the identification work.

Following route assistance could leave the camera facing structures or threats behind the player; manual turning was needed to locate the perimeter patrol. Route assistance did not remove shield damage near Custodian.
Final coil fire exhausted the magazine in both runs, requiring reload delay and a fresh aim; timing between armor/open windows and cover was harder to judge than the large objective HUD.
Attempt-one second deck burst spent one round without a down confirmation; terminal accuracy 97% shows imperfect fire overall but does not identify which bullet missed.
DASH activation/cooldown observed in both attempts; zero recorded phase evades. Its defensive effectiveness and human comfort remain unproven.

Tap aim and assisted fire made short engagements tractable; this does not prove free aiming accuracy, sustained manual combat, aim toggle comfort, KIT usability, JUMP behavior or enjoyment of unassessed content.

scores.scale: 0 unusable, 5 functional with substantial friction, 7 good with noticeable limits, 9 excellent, 10 exceptional. Subjective holistic assessment of observed emulated mobile play; wins and terminal scores are not quality grades. Overall is judgment, not arithmetic.

reasons.overallMobile: Coherent, attractive short mission with helpful navigation and combat feedback; manual combat sample is small and assisted, with target visibility and orientation friction.
reasons.controls: MOVE plus FIRE drag, scene swipe and DASH accepted inputs, with clear labels. Fine aim, continuous holds and successful evasive DASH not established.
reasons.gameplay: Recoveries, coil encounter and uplink offer a clear sequence and different tasks. Reload corrections and active patrols create demands, but route-heavy paused play limits assessment of pacing and combat depth.
reasons.presentation: Strong teal/amber identity, rainy industrial setting and polished title/result screens observed. Audio and hardware rendering unassessed.
reasons.usability: Persistent mission checks, contextual hold action, map route and explicit terminal assist stats aid understanding. Route orientation and repeated contextual holds still need attention.
reasons.readability: Main objective, ammo and progress are clear. Small world labels/distant targets, dark geometry and multiple competing HUD cues are harder on 390px width.
